definitions.explanation: The system of formal and polite expressions in Japanese used to show respect to others or humility about oneself.

examples.japanese: {敬語|けいご}を{正|ただ}しく{使|つか}うのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It's difficult to use honorific language correctly.

examples.japanese: {目上|めうえ}の{人|ひと}には{敬語|けいご}で{話|はな}す。
examples.english: Speak to superiors using honorific language.

examples.japanese: {敬語|けいご}が{上手|じょうず}だと{印象|いんしょう}がいい。
examples.english: Being skilled at honorific language makes a good impression.

notes:
TYPES OF KEIGO:
・{尊敬語|そんけいご} (honorific language - elevates the listener/subject)
・{謙譲語|けんじょうご} (humble language - lowers the speaker)
・{丁寧語|ていねいご} (polite language - です/ます forms)

EXAMPLES:
・{食|た}べる → {召|め}し{上|あ}がる (honorific), いただく (humble)
・{言|い}う → おっしゃる (honorific), {申|もう}す (humble)
・{行|い}く → いらっしゃる (honorific), {参|まい}る (humble)

USAGE: Essential in Japanese business, service industry, and formal social interactions. Many Japanese people struggle with keigo even as adults.
